runs.note: PPO from a random network, no imitation. The evaluation games (GA base, bots) are only measured, never trained on, until a stage adds those opponents.

decisions.title: Start from random weights, no imitation
decisions.text: rl-v2 tests whether the GA genome is a head start or a ceiling: same network, inputs and PPO as rl-v1, only the start changes. Self-play first, then the bots, then every earlier model.
decisions.rejected: Imitation first (that is rl-v1); a new architecture (would mix two changes into one comparison).

decisions.title: Stage 1 ends on a plateau, not a score
decisions.text: The first start ended self-play after 12 iterations, when it beat the bots 50% of the time. Self-play is the point of the project, so stage 1 now runs until the score against the GA genome has not improved for 60 iterations (at most 400): it shows how far self-play gets alone.
decisions.rejected: A fixed bots threshold (ended the stage after 3 minutes); a fixed iteration count (could stop while it is still learning, or waste hours on a plateau).

decisions.title: 1,500 games per iteration
decisions.text: Random players make long games with ~210 decisions each; 3,000 of them (rl-v1's setting) ran the 8 GB laptop out of memory. 1,500 fit with room for the evaluation.
decisions.rejected: Keeping 3,000 with float16 features (a change to the shared code that rl-v1 does not have).

decisions.title: Same evaluation games as rl-v1
decisions.text: The per-iteration evaluation and the goal checks use rl-v1's and az-v1's seeds, so every number compares directly with them. A new confirmation seed is kept for the end.
